summary: Makoto Funaoka works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Meiji University (~1965–1969, ~1971–1977) and served as a lecturer at The Open University of Japan and Komazawa University, and professor emeritus at Hokkai-Gakuen University (1993–2017).

Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Makoto Kitada completed doctoral studies at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held a post at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010) and is attested at Osaka University (2026).

Makoto Nagai was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1934–1942), Nihon, Toyo, and Kamakura Women's universities, and president of Chuo Shoka Junior College (1951).
Makoto Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1995–2000). He held an assistant professorship at Komazawa University around 2004.
Malati J. Shendge is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, R. D. Vadekar, and Akira Hirakawa.

Malay Porey, an Indologist and linguist, earned an M.A. from Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute (2012–2014). He served as Assistant Professor at Durgapur Government College (2016), Government General Degree College, Ranibandh (2020–2025), and Acharya Brojendra Nath Seal College (2025).

Malcolm David Eckel is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oxford and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served at Harvard (1980–1991) and was Associate Professor of Religion at Boston University (1990–2024).
Malcolm Huxter, working in Buddhist studies and psychology, earned a B.A. (Hons) from the University of New England (1985–1991) and a Master of Psychology from Charles Sturt University (1998–2002).
Malcolm Stuart Haughton Thompson was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Principal of Government College, Rajahmundry (1931–1932) and held an academic post at SOAS University of London.
Malcolm Voyce is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who was educated at the University of London. He served as a professor at Macquarie University (attested 2009).

Mallica Kumbera Landrus specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She holds posts attested in 2026 as Keeper of Eastern Art at the Ashmolean Museum and Associate Professor of Indian Art at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.
Mamata Dash is a scholar in the field of Indology who completed her education at Ravenshaw Girls' School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki. He held posts at Kyoto University from 1965 to 2001, Kobe University (1971), and Otani University (2003).
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as Co-ordinator for DSA Sanskrit at Jadavpur University (attested 2003) and as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society.

Manabu Asano is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed PhD studies at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020) and is attested as a researcher at Minobusan University (2026).
Manasi Dilip Nadkarni is an Indologist and linguist who studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya. She is attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Manasicha Akepiyapornchai is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed a master's at Cornell University (2014–2022). In 2022, she was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of Texas at Austin.

Mandan Mishra was an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as Principal and Chief Editor at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University (~1967–1989), Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1996–1999), and held a post at the University of Rajasthan.

Manfred Mayrhofer, a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, earned his Ph.D. and Habilitation at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein. He was a full professor at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

Manfred Taube was a Tibetologist, Indologist, and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Leipzig (1949–1953) under Friedrich Weller. In 1991, he became Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology at the University of Leipzig.
